newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar settles lower and within range.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar settles lower and within range.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed weaker and within their recent trading range ahead of the May contract's expiry Wednesday, dealers said.
The trade continued to roll short May positions into July, pushing the nearby spread as wide as 0.47 at one point, before it settled at 0.42.

The trade was also a noted buyer scale-down in July, supporting the contract above 11.00 cents a lb. Further support was noted at Friday's low of 10.91 cents, under which sell stops may be lurking, dealers said.
Producer selling is expected to limit gains over 11.18-11.20 cents in July.
The most-active month finished down 0.07 cent at 11.07 cents after trading from 11.12 to 11.01 cents. Spot May eased 0.06 to 11.49, while the back months ended 0.06 to 0.03 lower.
Turnover was estimated at 21,323 lots compared with Friday's official 17,623 lots.
Open interest in May fell 1,533 lots, remaining high at 24,774 lots, as of early Friday. July gained 298 lots to stand at 85,769 lots.

Players are expected to begin to address the heavy speculative long position in July once the spot month expires, market sources said. The Commitment of Traders Report, released after the close Friday, showed the speculators to be holding about 66,500 longs as of last Tuesday's close.
"It just confirms what we suspected and that may have prompted weakness in July," a dealer said.
He said a move below 10.77 cents, the recent low basis July hit on April 17, could trigger speculative liquidation.
((-- S Rostler, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640))
